original_test_intent: Verify N+1 PSU redundancy and hot-service behavior at approved full-system load across five cycles per PSU, including input/removal state, BMC/SEL accuracy, visible indicators, workload continuity and full recovery.
original_method: Map each PSU serial/slot to its AC feed and BMC sensors, prove survivor capacity against measured load, start an approved bounded full-system workload, then have a qualified operator perform cord-off, module-out, module-in and cord-on checkpoints while automation records power, thermal, workload and event continuity.
manual_activity: Qualified operator identifies the exact PSU/feed, unplugs and reconnects its AC cord, removes/reinserts the module, and confirms fan/LED state under an approved service procedure.
required_inputs: Measured peak load and survivor capacity
safety_requirements: Require explicit approval for full-load AC/PSU removal
Verify N+1 margin before each cycle
Never guess a PSU or feed
Remove only one approved PSU/feed at a time
Maintain independent BMC and PDU observation
Stop on brownout, reset, throttling, thermal excursion or module fault
Do not continue after failed reinsertion or degraded redundancy
agent_execution_scope: Inventory PSU serials/slots/feeds and baseline sensors
Measure load and calculate survivor margin
Guide but never perform physical actions
Capture AC-loss, absent, inserted and AC-restored checkpoints
Monitor BMC/SEL, host, GPU, storage, fans, PCIe and USB continuity
engineer_actions: Resolve any power or continuity anomaly

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsblk, mdadm, storcli and generic dmesg monitoring are unrelated to the core PSU removal, power redundancy, BMC sensor/SEL and module-continuity requirements.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the approved full-system workload only after capacity proof; for each PSU and each of five cycles, capture four physical-state checkpoints plus synchronized BMC/SEL, power, thermal, workload and module-health evidence, stopping on the first anomaly.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Full CPU/DIMM/GPU/HDD load, cord-off/module-out/module-in/cord-on order, all PSUs, five repetitions and 30/30-minute timing are preserved; feed and stress parameters are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a PSU-cycle ledger keyed by serial/slot/feed with measured input/output power, redundancy margin, BMC state transitions, SEL correlation, workload continuity and restored-state dwell.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds quantitative capacity and synchronized transition evidence to the physical sequence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-feed pulls, insufficient redundancy, transient workload interruption, stale PSU telemetry and incomplete failback.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Nameplate ratings do not prove dynamic survivor margin; PDU/feed topology errors can convert a one-PSU test into a full outage.

project_override_considerations: The phrase 'full loading stress' requires a versioned project stress profile and measured power envelope. The private SEL script may supplement but cannot establish PSU/feed identity or module continuity until reviewed.
expected_evidence: Measured baseline/peak load and survivor margin
PDU input and PSU output telemetry
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target redundant PSU hot-service under load. Missing feed mapping, capacity and stress definition are execution prerequisites, not contradictory source meaning.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The PSU identities, capacity calculation, workload and recovery are finite project/lab inputs. Unsafe capacity or irrecoverable power topology after request would block execution.

review_improvement: Replaces an unrelated storage plan with a measurable PSU redundancy test and prevents a guessed feed or insufficient survivor capacity from causing an outage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PSU hot-service test is safe only when the remaining modules and independent AC path can carry the measured load with transient margin. Cord removal and module extraction create distinct BMC states and must be time-correlated. The physical operations require a qualified operator, while telemetry and continuity checks are automatable; therefore REQUIRES, not PARTIAL-as-command or MANUAL ONLY, is appropriate.
